evidence: ThreatFabric's technical analysis published 2026-10-14 lists com.agbbh.kjdrttt, com.onev.vip, com.koishort.app, and com.zoyatv.app as Hirudo lure/dropper packages, and com.zk7qpx.mv9wlt and com.r9nkvx.qw2mpl as Hirudo RAT payload packages. It documents the droppers installing the payload and the RAT's credential theft, SMS collection, and remote-control behavior. The article pairs these package names with sample SHA-256s but does not provide signing-certificate SHA-1s. Source: https://www.threatfabric.com/blogs/hirudo-from-fake-updates-to-patched-banking-apps
